title: After hours
brief: 18:50. The door intercom buzzes. A courier wants to be let in. And there is that USB stick from the car park.
insight: Reception closed at six. Anyone at the door after that is your decision, and your risk.
teaches: after hours, nobody is let in without a check
security deals with visitors, not you alone
an unknown USB stick is handed in, never plugged in

card.title: Someone at the lobby door
card.imageAlt: A grainy camera still of a courier in a hi vis vest holding a parcel at the lobby door
body: A courier in a hi vis vest, holding a parcel. “Delivery for the finance team, I just need someone to buzz me in, my hands are full.”
Reception is closed. There is no delivery expected. Buzzing them in puts a stranger on the finance floor, out of hours, with nobody around.

choices.label: Call security to deal with it
Buzz them in, they have their hands full
There’s a courier at the lobby door wanting in
I found a USB stick in the car park

script.say: Do not buzz anyone in. There is no delivery booked tonight. I will come down and check the camera myself.
Good call not plugging it in. Leave it in an envelope at the IT desk, or log a ticket and I will collect it.

setup.title: Door intercom
setup.body: A courier is at the lobby door

outcome.label: Called security about the courier
outcome.what: Security check the camera and handle the door. That is their job, not yours to guess at.
outcome.ideal: lets security handle an unexpected visitor rather than deciding alone.

outcome.label: Got security on the desk phone
outcome.what: Mo will come down and check. Nobody gets buzzed in.
outcome.ideal: uses the security line for anything physical after hours.

outcome.label: Handed the USB stick to IT unopened
outcome.what: A labelled stick in a car park is bait. Handing it in unopened costs nothing.
outcome.ideal: never plugs in a found device, and hands it to IT.

outcome.label: Logged it with the service desk
outcome.what: There is a record of the after hours visit and the found device.

door.step: Deal with the courier at the door
door.objective: Deal with the courier at the door.
door.insight: “My hands are full, just buzz me in” is a script. It works because refusing feels rude.

hint.text: Look at the intercom. Do not buzz them in. Call security on the desk phone (4999) to handle it.

outcome.label: Buzzed the stranger in
outcome.what: There is now an unknown person on the finance floor, after hours, with nobody around. That is how a device gets planted or a desk gets photographed.
outcome.ideal: never buzzes in an unexpected visitor after hours; calls security instead.

card.title: A stranger on the floor
body: You buzzed them in. The parcel was a prop. With the floor empty, a few minutes is enough to plug something into a spare port, photograph the whiteboard, or lift a document from a desk.
There was no delivery booked. Security exists for exactly this, and they were one call away.
card.ideal: refuses the door and calls security.

usb.step: Decide what to do with the USB stick
usb.objective: Decide what to do with the USB stick.
usb.insight: The label PAYROLL Q3 is chosen to make you curious enough to plug it in.

hint.text: Look at the USB stick and hand it to IT without plugging it in.

outcome.label: Plugged in the USB stick
outcome.what: The stick was left to be found. Plugging it in is exactly what its label was designed to make you do.
outcome.ideal: never plugs in a found device.

card.title: It was left to be found
body: The moment it was plugged in, the stick did its work. A dropped device with a tempting label is not lost property, it is bait.
Handing it to IT unopened was the whole job.
card.ideal: hands a found device to IT without plugging it in.
